intro: The Titans sent Jeffery Simmons to the Bears for two first-round picks, the biggest move before the Nov. 10 deadline so far. Sunday brings unbeaten Minnesota to Detroit and a Chiefs-Broncos game for first place in the AFC West, and Monday night puts Chicago in Seattle. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Bears trade two first-round picks for Jeffery Simmons
top.dek: Chicago sent its 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and a 2027 fourth to Tennessee for the All-Pro tackle, and gets a 2028 fifth back. Simmons leads all defensive tackles with 28 pressures, according to Next Gen Stats. The Titans are 1-6 and now have two more firsts to work with.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Rice nears return as Chiefs head to Denver
top.dek: Rashee Rice missed two games with a hamstring injury and practiced in a limited role. He is listed as questionable for Sunday. Patrick Mahomes said Rice's return would take pressure off the other receivers after the 20-3 loss at Seattle.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Jared Goff has 1,788 yards and no interceptions
top.dek: Goff has thrown for 14 touchdowns through six games without a pick. He faces a Vikings defense that blitzes constantly and allows the fewest points in the league. The Lions want to end Minnesota's 11-game winning streak on Sunday.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 12.3: points per game the Vikings allow, best in the NFL
top.dek: Minnesota also ranks second in total defense at 252.8 yards per game. Brian Flores blitzes at nearly a 70 percent rate. The offense has completed only 15 passes of 20 or more yards, 25th in the league.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Chiefs visit Broncos Sunday with first place in the AFC West at stake
top.dek: Kansas City (5-1) plays at 5-2 Denver at 4:25 PM ET on CBS. The Broncos lost the Week 1 opener 31-10 and call this a redemption game. Sean Payton coaches his 300th NFL game.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills try to patch a thin secondary vs Ravens

stories.text: Allen and Jackson meet again with the AFC lead at stake
stories.summary: The Bills (5-1) host the Ravens (4-3) on Sunday, tied with Kansas City for the best record in the AFC. Josh Allen is rested after the bye. Baltimore has lost two straight, including a 35-13 loss to Cincinnati after leading 13-0 at the half.

stories.text: Alford slides to no practice, Gardner-Johnson serves ban
stories.summary: Cornerback Dee Alford went from limited to sitting out Thursday and looks unlikely to play. Bradley Chubb and T.J. Parker were limited, while Ed Oliver and T.J. Sanders practiced in full. Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson is suspended, so Damar Hamlin is expected to start with rookie Jalon Kilgore getting snaps.

stories.text: Josh Allen is 2-0 in the playoffs against Lamar Jackson
stories.summary: Allen and Jackson split their four regular season meetings 2-2, and Allen owns both postseason matchups. Jackson holds two MVP awards to Allen's one. Allen comes off the bye with the league's top scoring offense around him.

stories.text: 285.8: Bills allow the second most passing yards a game
stories.summary: Buffalo's pass defense gives up 285.8 yards per game through the air, second most in the NFL. With a safety suspended and a cornerback likely out, a healthy Lamar Jackson has room to work on Sunday.

stories.text: Ravens visit Buffalo Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Bills return from their bye to face Baltimore at home. Watch how the pass rush handles Jackson and whether the thin secondary holds up. Buffalo plays at Minnesota on Monday night, Nov. 9, in Week 9.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins chase win No. 2 against old coach Vrabel

stories.text: Willis faces his old coach as Dolphins host the Patriots
stories.summary: Miami (1-5) hosts New England (4-3) on Sunday after its first win, 28-25 over the Jets. Quarterback Malik Willis played for Patriots coach Mike Vrabel in Tennessee, where the Titans drafted him in 2022. Willis threw for 208 yards and two scores and ran for another against the Jets.

stories.text: Proctor sits again in concussion protocol, Brents limited
stories.summary: Left guard Kadyn Proctor did not practice Thursday with a concussion. Cornerback JuJu Brents moved from no practice to limited with a neck and concussion designation. Several others were limited, including tight ends Greg Dulcich and Will Kacmarek and safety Michael Taaffe.

stories.text: Ollie Gordon has scored a rushing TD in four straight games
stories.summary: The Miami running back has found the end zone on the ground in each of the last four games. He leads a ground game that has topped 100 yards five weeks in a row.

stories.text: 5: straight Dolphins games with 100 rushing yards
stories.summary: No team in the league has a longer streak. Miami averages 131.5 rushing yards a game, seventh in the NFL, even though its 16.3 points per game ranks 30th. New England's run defense ranks eighth at 95.3 yards allowed.

stories.text: Patriots visit Miami Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami has not allowed a rushing touchdown in three straight games, the longest run in the league. New England beat the Dolphins 38-10 in their last meeting on Jan. 4. The Dolphins host Detroit on Nov. 8 in Week 9.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots get secondary back, A.J. Brown in doubt

stories.text: Patriots expect full secondary for first time since Week 1
stories.summary: Cornerbacks Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III and safeties Kevin Byard and Craig Woodson are expected back at Miami. Davis missed four games with a neck injury and Gonzalez missed two with a shoulder injury. New England (4-3) is a 7.5 point favorite against the 1-5 Dolphins.

stories.text: A.J. Brown skips Thursday practice with knee flare-up
stories.summary: Brown did not practice Thursday after a knee problem flared, and Ian Rapoport reported his Sunday status is up in the air. He also carries an ankle designation from the injury that put him on injured reserve after Week 1. Running back TreVeyon Henderson missed practice with an illness.

stories.text: Hunter Henry is one touchdown from third on a Patriots list
stories.summary: Henry has 28 career touchdown catches for New England. One more moves him into sole possession of third place among Patriots tight ends.

stories.text: 29-33: Patriots' record against Miami since 2000
stories.summary: Miami leads the all-time series 63-55, but the Patriots scored more than 30 points in both wins over the Dolphins last season.

stories.text: Patriots at Dolphins Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: New England looks to bounce back from its 30-24 loss at Chicago. Watch how the Patriots replace Brown's targets if he sits. They host Green Bay on Nov. 8 in Week 9.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Geno Smith faces former team as Jets host Raiders

stories.text: Geno Smith faces the Raiders for the first time since exit
stories.summary: The Jets (2-5) host Las Vegas (3-4) on Sunday after a 28-25 loss to winless Miami. The Raiders have lost four straight and rank 29th in total defense at about 373.7 yards allowed per game. Smith ranks third in the league in completion percentage at 70.0.

stories.text: Allen back to full, Hall limited again with quad
stories.summary: Braelon Allen moved from limited to full Thursday with his ankle. Breece Hall (quad) and guard Dylan Parham (knee) were limited for a second day. Edge David Bailey, lineman Max Mitchell, edge Joseph Ossai and lineman T'Vondre Sweat did not practice, and Aaron Glenn called Sweat and Ossai week to week.

stories.text: Braelon Allen: 357 rushing yards in four starts
stories.summary: That total is the second most in the NFL over that stretch. Allen also has 56 receiving yards in the last two games, and he is healthy enough to practice in full.

stories.text: 373.7: yards per game the Raiders defense allows
stories.summary: Las Vegas ranks 29th in total defense. Its offense has no 100-yard rusher since Week 3, and the Rams held it to 49 rushing yards in Week 7.

stories.text: Raiders visit MetLife Sunday at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Jets try to snap a two game skid. Watch the running game and whether Hall returns. New York travels to Kansas City on Nov. 8 for Week 9.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Jackson logs a second full practice before Buffalo

stories.text: Lamar Jackson practices fully again, Bills game looms
stories.summary: Jackson took full reps for the second straight day on Thursday after missing three games with a left ankle sprain. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said the staff is running game-speed practices so Jackson can pick up where he left off. Baltimore has lost two straight to division rivals and sits at 4-3.

stories.text: Ioane, Hamilton and Smith return to practice
stories.summary: Right guard Vega Ioane practiced on a limited basis four days after a reported MCL sprain, and coach Jesse Minter did not rule him out for Buffalo. Safety Kyle Hamilton and linebacker Roquan Smith, both resting knees on Wednesday, also practiced. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) was the only Raven who did not take part.

stories.text: Derrick Henry leans on 579 yards and seven scores
stories.summary: Henry has 579 rushing yards on 147 carries, a 3.9 average, with seven rushing touchdowns. The ground game is the steadier piece of an offense that leaned on Tyler Huntley for three starts. Henry's workload is the number to watch if Jackson plays.

stories.text: 7-13: Baltimore's record without Lamar Jackson
stories.summary: The Ravens are 7-13 all-time in games Jackson does not play. Huntley made three starts in his absence. Reporter Ian Rapoport said Jackson is past the two-to-three week window and near 100 percent.

stories.text: At Buffalo, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Ravens visit a 5-1 Bills team that leads the NFL in scoring at 32.8 points per game and is coming off its bye. Baltimore averages 24.1. Watch whether Jackson starts and whether the Ravens can keep Buffalo's offense off the field with Henry.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Chase returns to full practice after ankle scare

stories.text: Ja'Marr Chase back at full practice after ankle scare
stories.summary: Chase sat out Wednesday with a rest and ankle designation, then went full on Thursday. Cincinnati never listed him in danger of missing the Titans game. He has 32 catches for 351 yards and five touchdowns through six games.

stories.text: Kyle Dugger sits again; Giles-Harris slips
stories.summary: Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, and coach Zac Taylor has said he will not play Sunday. Linebacker Joe Giles-Harris went from limited to not practicing with a calf issue. Jordan Battle (hamstring) stayed limited.

stories.text: Joe Burrow leads the NFL in completion rate
stories.summary: Burrow completes 71.4 percent of his passes, tops in the league, with a 110.4 passer rating and 15 touchdown passes. He threw four touchdowns without an interception in each of the last two games. A year ago at this time he was recovering from turf toe surgery.

stories.text: 22: Evan McPherson's franchise-record field goal streak
stories.summary: McPherson has made 22 straight field goals, a team record. The Bengals defense also ties for the league lead with 21 sacks despite blitzing on just 18.5 percent of snaps. Both numbers feed a 4-2 start that is only the second time Zac Taylor has had a winning record after six games.

stories.text: Home against Tennessee, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The 1-6 Titans traded defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to Chicago on Thursday. Cincinnati is a double-digit favorite and four of its five November opponents have losing records. Watch rookie Carnell Tate, who leads NFL rookies in catches, and his shoulder status.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns chase a sweep in Pittsburgh at 5-2

stories.text: Browns are 5-2 with one of the league's thinnest margins
stories.summary: Cleveland has won five games while being outscored by 13 points, one of the weakest point differentials for a 5-2 team since 2000. Five of those wins came on fourth-quarter drives. The Browns have not started 5-2 since 2020 and visit Pittsburgh on Sunday.

stories.text: Tytus Howard still out with a concussion
stories.summary: Right tackle Tytus Howard did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, and the depth chart has Dawand Jones next up. Defensive end Jared Verse (knee) and center Elgton Jenkins (knee) moved from no practice to limited Thursday. Defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. (ankles) stayed limited.

stories.text: Quinshon Judkins scores twice in Tennessee
stories.summary: Judkins ran 17 times for a season-high 96 yards and touchdowns of 5 and 6 yards. Dylan Sampson added 45 yards on six carries. The Browns finished with 183 rushing yards at 6.3 per carry.

stories.text: 52: Games since a Browns opponent threw for 300
stories.summary: Cleveland has gone 52 straight games without allowing a 300-yard passer, the longest active streak in the NFL. Tennessee's Cam Ward threw for 181 yards on Sunday. Aaron Rodgers threw for 299 in the first meeting with Pittsburgh.

stories.text: At Pittsburgh, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Both teams are 5-2 and Cleveland won the first meeting 27-24. Pittsburgh has lost at home to the Browns only once since Acrisure Stadium opened in 2001. Watch the Browns' offensive line, which could start rookies Spencer Fano and Austin Barber.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers fix the red zone before Browns rematch

stories.text: Steelers admit red zone offense must improve
stories.summary: Pittsburgh ranks 27th in red zone offense, and coach Mike McCarthy said the team needs more touchdowns inside the 20. A win Sunday would give the Steelers a fourth straight victory and sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Cleveland beat them 27-24 in Week 4.

stories.text: Ramsey goes full; two defensive backs still out
stories.summary: Cornerback Jalen Ramsey returned to full practice Thursday after sitting out Wednesday with a wrist injury. Cornerback Brandin Echols and defensive back Doneiko Slaughter, both with hamstrings, missed both days. Linebacker Alex Highsmith (groin) and receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) were limited both days.

stories.text: Aaron Rodgers passes Peyton Manning for third in TDs
stories.summary: Rodgers threw a 4-yard touchdown to Darnell Washington in Paris, his 540th career touchdown pass, which moved him past Peyton Manning for third all time. He finished 19 of 30 for 212 yards in the 16-10 win over New Orleans. The offense still needs more from the red zone.

stories.text: 1: Home losses to Cleveland since 2001
stories.summary: Pittsburgh has lost only once at home to the Browns since Acrisure Stadium opened in 2001. The Steelers lead the all-time series 83-66-1. Cleveland did beat them in Week 4 this season.

stories.text: Home against Cleveland, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The 5-2 Steelers host the 5-2 Browns in a game that decides who leads the AFC North. Pittsburgh got back from Paris early Monday, so practice began Wednesday. Safety DeShon Elliott played 19 snaps in his return and his workload is still to be set.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Caserio keeps the Texans open for deadline deals

stories.text: Caserio says Texans won't rule out any deadline move
stories.summary: General manager Nick Caserio said Houston has talked with most of the league and will not eliminate any option before the Nov. 10 deadline. He also warned against knee-jerk decisions after the overtime loss to the Giants. The Texans already added receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. from Arizona for a 2027 second-round pick, and they sit 0-4 at home.

stories.text: Montgomery's groin gets the bye week to heal
stories.summary: Running back David Montgomery missed the Giants game with a groin injury and did not practice that week. Coach DeMeco Ryans calls it week-to-week with no firm return date. The bye gives him extra time before the Nov. 8 game at the Chargers.

stories.text: Nico Collins went quiet in the loss to the Giants
stories.summary: Collins caught two passes for six yards in Houston's overtime loss to New York. Locked On Texans host John Hickman faulted the offense for ignoring Collins in the fourth quarter and overtime. With Jaylin Noel on injured reserve, the Texans need their top receiver back in the game plan.

stories.text: 2.7: David Montgomery's yards per carry this season
stories.summary: Montgomery has 138 rushing yards on 52 carries with two touchdowns. His best game came in Week 1, when he scored three times on 20 carries. He has struggled since.

stories.text: Bye in Week 8, then at the Chargers on Nov. 8
stories.summary: Houston is off this Sunday. The Texans visit the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:05 PM ET on CBS. The Chargers are 0-6. The Texans then travel to Cleveland in Week 10.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Taylor says he never asked out of Indianapolis

stories.text: Jonathan Taylor says he has not asked for a trade
stories.summary: Taylor told reporters he has not requested a trade and is proud to wear the horseshoe, though he admitted the business side can change fast. Several teams have asked Indianapolis about his availability, and the Colts have not said where they stand. He signed an extension in August that runs through 2028.

stories.text: Gardner returns to full practice, Warren still limited
stories.summary: Cornerback Sauce Gardner moved to full participation Thursday after missing the Vikings game with a calf strain. Tight end Tyler Warren, who has missed two games with a groin injury, was limited. Linebacker Bryce Boettcher and cornerback Justin Walley did not practice for a second straight day.

stories.text: Josh Downs asks out with a team-high 307 yards
stories.summary: Downs asked the Colts for a trade after the Nelson and Buckner deals. Through seven games he has 26 catches on 46 targets for 307 yards, the most on the team, with no touchdowns. He says he is focused on Jacksonville, and he is on an expiring rookie contract.

stories.text: 85%: how often Minnesota blitzed Daniel Jones
stories.summary: The Vikings sent extra rushers on 85 percent of Jones's dropbacks in a 16-10 Colts loss. Indianapolis scored only 10 points. Jacksonville blitzes on fewer than 40 percent of pass attempts, so Jones may see a different look Sunday.

stories.text: At Jacksonville Sunday, then home for Dallas
stories.summary: The Colts visit the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:00 PM ET on CBS, looking to end a three-game losing streak. Jacksonville is 4-2 and coming off a bye. Indianapolis hosts Dallas on Nov. 8 at 1:00 PM ET on Fox.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. tunes out trade talk before Colts

stories.text: Brian Thomas Jr. tries to block out trade buzz
stories.summary: Thomas said he wants to flush his rough showing against Houston in London and keep working. Coach Liam Coen called him a significant part of the offense and expects him to make plays Sunday against the Colts. Thomas has nine catches for 105 yards and a touchdown in six games, with four drops.

stories.text: Harrison is done, Little takes over at left tackle
stories.summary: Left tackle Anton Harrison is out for the season with a torn ACL. Walker Little makes his second start of the year in his place, and Jacksonville says the job is his for the rest of 2026. The staff tries to keep at least eight starting-caliber linemen, which softens the loss.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence has a career-best 14 touchdown passes
stories.summary: Lawrence has thrown 14 touchdown passes through six games, the most he has had at this point in any season. He passed for 306 yards and four scores against Houston in the last outing. He gets a Colts defense that just lost Buckner.

stories.text: Under 40%: how often the Jaguars blitz
stories.summary: Defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile sends extra rushers on fewer than 40 percent of pass attempts. That contrasts with Minnesota, which blitzed Daniel Jones on 85 percent of his dropbacks last week. Jacksonville allowed 17, 17 and 6 points in the three games before Houston scored 34.

stories.text: Colts at EverBank Sunday, then Baltimore on Thursday
stories.summary: Jacksonville hosts Indianapolis on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. They then visit Baltimore on Thursday night, Nov. 5, at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans trade Jeffery Simmons to Chicago

stories.text: Titans trade Jeffery Simmons to the Bears for two firsts
stories.summary: Tennessee sent Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick to Chicago for the Bears' 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and a 2027 fourth. Simmons was a 2019 first-round pick, a four-time Pro Bowler and a five-time team captain. Owner Amy Adams Strunk said few people are like him.

stories.text: Spears, Tate and Townsend miss two straight practices
stories.summary: Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Receiver Calvin Ridley was limited with a hip issue and lineman John Franklin-Myers was limited Thursday. Friday designations were not posted yet.

stories.text: Tony Pollard ran for three scores against Cleveland
stories.summary: Pollard carried 25 times for 129 yards and three touchdowns in the 27-24 loss to the Browns, his best game of the season. He is 29 and in the final year of his contract, so his name is out there ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline. He sat out Thursday's practice for rest.

stories.text: 1-4: Tennessee's record in one-score games
stories.summary: Four of the Titans' six losses came by six points or fewer, including last week's 27-24 defeat to Cleveland. Their point differential is minus-48. Coach Robert Saleh said of the margin, "It is so close, it is so close."

stories.text: At Cincinnati Sunday, then a Week 9 bye
stories.summary: The Titans visit the 4-2 Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. Tennessee then has its bye in Week 9 and hosts Jacksonville on Nov. 15 at 1:00 PM ET on Fox. Quarterback Cam Ward has four touchdown passes through seven games.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos want redemption and the AFC West lead

stories.text: Broncos chase redemption against Chiefs
stories.summary: Denver lost the Week 1 opener 31-10 at Arrowhead, and players are calling Sunday a redemption game. A win would put the 5-2 Broncos in first place in the AFC West. They have won four of the last six against Kansas City.

stories.text: Allen and Waddle return to limited work
stories.summary: Defensive lineman Zach Allen (hamstring) and receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) sat out Wednesday, then practiced on a limited basis Thursday. Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice either day. Tackle Garett Bolles (hip) was limited both days, and final game statuses come Friday.

stories.text: Singleton leads the NFL with 87 tackles
stories.summary: Linebacker Alex Singleton tops the league in tackles through seven games. He anchors a Denver defense that ranks fourth in EPA allowed and has 21 sacks, even with injuries in the secondary. He faces a Chiefs run game that piled up yards on the Broncos in September.

stories.text: 5.8: Nix's yards per attempt, 7.7 for Mahomes
stories.summary: Bo Nix averages 5.8 yards per attempt and completes 59.2 percent of his passes, the lowest rate of his three-year career. Patrick Mahomes averages 7.7. Nix does rank third among qualifiers in pressure-to-sack rate and has 110 rushing yards.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Denver Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City (5-1) plays at Empower Field with first place in the AFC West at stake. Sean Payton will coach his 300th NFL game. Watch whether Denver tackles better after missing 28 tackles in the Week 1 loss.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Rice may return as Chiefs hunt a Denver rematch

stories.text: Rice nears return as Chiefs head to Denver
stories.summary: Receiver Rashee Rice missed two games with a hamstring injury and practiced in a limited role Wednesday. He is listed as questionable for Sunday. Patrick Mahomes said having Rice back should take pressure off the other receivers after the 20-3 loss at Seattle.

stories.text: Delane misses Thursday, Moore back on the line
stories.summary: Cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) did not practice Thursday. Tackle Jaylon Moore, who was in concussion protocol, practiced fully both days. Rice was limited on Wednesday and Thursday.

stories.text: Walker ran for 173 on Denver in Week 1
stories.summary: Running back Kenneth Walker III gashed the Broncos for 173 rushing yards in the 31-10 opener at Arrowhead. He brings 701 rushing yards on 5.8 per carry into the rematch. Denver missed 28 tackles in that first game.

stories.text: 2: straight games without a Mahomes TD pass
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes has gone consecutive games without a touchdown pass, a first in his career, according to CBS Sports. He threw for 165 yards and an interception in the 20-3 loss at Seattle. For the season he has 9 touchdowns and 4 interceptions.

stories.text: At Denver on Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Chiefs try to rebound from their first loss against a 5-2 Broncos team that wants revenge for Week 1. Kansas City leads the all-time series 74-59. Watch the Chiefs' pass protection and whether Rice plays.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Kubiak sticks with Cousins to stop the skid

stories.text: Kubiak keeps Cousins over rookie Mendoza
stories.summary: Klint Kubiak said there is no quarterback controversy and Kirk Cousins starts Sunday at the Jets. Rookie Fernando Mendoza waits behind him. The Raiders (3-4) have lost four straight and allowed 35.8 points per game during the skid.

stories.text: Johnson out with a stinger, Bowers still limited
stories.summary: Edge rusher Patrick Johnson missed Wednesday's practice with a stinger. Tight end Brock Bowers (calf), tackle DJ Glaze (ankle), linebacker Quay Walker (chest) and tight end Ian Thomas (shoulder) were limited. Bowers has 34 catches for 455 yards in five games.

stories.text: Cousins has 16 TDs and 5 picks for Las Vegas
stories.summary: Kirk Cousins threw for 295 yards and two touchdowns in the loss to the Rams. Kubiak says he is playing at a very high level. The Raiders rank seventh in scoring at 26.1 points per game.

stories.text: 199: rushing yards the Rams ran for on Las Vegas
stories.summary: The Rams ran for 199 yards in their 35-21 win, and the Raiders have allowed 416.5 total yards per game during the losing streak. Linebacker Nakobe Dean said the defense has to pick it up and he will hold teammates accountable. The Jets lean on Braelon Allen, who has 357 rushing yards over four games.

stories.text: At the Jets on Sunday, 1:00 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Las Vegas plays at MetLife Stadium against a 2-5 Jets team that lost 28-25 to Miami last week. The Raiders need their run defense to hold up against Allen. Watch whether Bowers is at full speed.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Derwin James faces IR as Chargers seek a win

stories.text: Derwin James may land on injured reserve
stories.summary: Safety Derwin James had a setback in his hamstring rehab, and Jim Harbaugh said he could go on injured reserve. He did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. The winless Chargers lose their top defender as they head to the Rams.

stories.text: McConkey practices fully after concussion
stories.summary: Receiver Ladd McConkey was a full participant Wednesday and Thursday. Tackle Kayode Awosika (fibula), cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) and receiver Brenen Thompson did not practice. Tre Harris, Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley (all hamstring) were limited.

stories.text: Herbert has 8 interceptions and 5 touchdowns
stories.summary: Justin Herbert has thrown more interceptions than touchdowns this season, and his passer rating ranks second worst in the NFL. The Chargers have allowed 21 sacks, third most in the league. He faces a Rams team with only 10 sacks.

stories.text: 21: sacks the Chargers have allowed
stories.summary: Only two teams have given up more sacks. The Los Angeles offense scores about 15 points per game, and the defense allows 25.2. The Chargers have forced 10 turnovers and rank in the top 10 in red-zone defense.

stories.text: At the Rams on Sunday, 4:05 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Chargers (0-6) are the only winless team in the NFL and visit a 3-4 Rams team at SoFi Stadium. Watch whether Joe Alt and McConkey help the offense find a rhythm.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys defense tries to back up the Eagles win

stories.text: Cowboys defense faces a consistency test against Arizona
stories.summary: Dallas has six of its 10 sacks over the last three games and both of its interceptions over the last two. Quinnen Williams and Joey Porter Jr. have driven that, and the staff added defensive assistant Mike Pettine. The Eagles still put up 21 points, so the Cowboys want proof the defense can hold up for a full game.

stories.text: Schoonmaker joins Turpin and Winters on the injury list
stories.summary: Tight end Luke Schoonmaker (groin) was added Thursday, and receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and linebacker Dee Winters (calf) missed a second straight day. Quinnen Williams (hamstring) and Caleb Downs (ankle) were limited, as were George Pickens and Drew Shelton. Game designations arrive with Friday's report.

stories.text: Dak Prescott chases his first win over Arizona since 2017
stories.summary: Prescott threw three touchdown passes and no interceptions in the win over Philadelphia. He is 1-3 against the Cardinals, and his only win came in 2017. Dallas leans on him to keep that efficiency up against a team that has beaten the Cowboys four straight times.

stories.text: 8: rushing TDs for Javonte Williams, tied for NFL lead
stories.summary: Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards and a score against the Eagles. He enters Week 8 tied for the league lead with eight rushing touchdowns. Dallas entered Week 7 ranked 31st in rushing offense, so his production changed the shape of the offense.

stories.text: Sunday: Cardinals visit Arlington at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Dallas hosts Arizona at AT&T Stadium on Sunday at 1 PM ET on Fox. The Cardinals have won four straight in the series and have never lost at AT&T Stadium since it opened in 2009. Watch whether Arizona running back Jeremiyah Love returns from his injury.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants sit atop the NFC East heading into the bye

stories.text: Giants hold the NFC East lead into their bye week
stories.summary: New York sits at 4-2-1 and keeps first place no matter what happens Sunday. John Harbaugh is 15-3 in games right after a bye, and he called the Eagles trip and the home game against Washington days later the biggest of the season so far. General manager Joe Schoen says the staff will weigh trade options before the Nov. 10 deadline.

stories.text: Tyrone Tracy lands on IR with a hamstring injury
stories.summary: The running back is expected to miss at least four games, with Week 13 against San Francisco the earliest return. The Giants signed Gregory Desrosiers from the Chargers practice squad. Harbaugh said earlier that the team has a lot of small bumps and the bye comes at a good time.

stories.text: Isaiah Likely has 41 catches, one shy of his career high
stories.summary: The tight end is on pace for 100 receptions through seven games. He has become a steady target for whichever quarterback starts, and the Giants have won with three different ones. The offense has scored at least 27 points in four straight games, its longest run since 2010.

stories.text: 32.9%: Giants defense forces three-and-outs, best in NFL
stories.summary: The Giants ended 26 of 79 opponent drives in three plays or fewer. Seattle is second at 30.4%. The offense ranks third in time of possession at 32:35 per game, which helps the defense rest.

stories.text: On bye now, then Nov. 8 at Philadelphia, 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: New York is off this weekend and returns Monday to prepare for the Eagles. The Giants have lost 13 straight in Philadelphia, with the last win coming on Oct. 27, 2013. They follow with a home game against Washington on Thursday night, Nov. 12.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Sirianni says effort is not the Eagles' problem

stories.text: Sirianni says effort is not the problem in Philadelphia
stories.summary: The coach rejected the idea of an effort issue two days after the fifth straight loss, saying film showed no breakdown of that kind. Former quarterback Nick Foles said on a podcast that team culture is a problem, and Sirianni answered that Foles is not in the building. The Eagles try to snap the skid on Sunday night in Washington.

stories.text: Six Eagles sit again, and Hurts is out for the year
stories.summary: Running back Saquon Barkley, receiver DeVonta Smith, receiver Dontayvion Wicks, linebacker Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey and cornerback Jonathan Jones sat out Wednesday and Thursday. Wednesday was a walkthrough, so that report was an estimate. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the season after doctors found blood clots in his lungs.

stories.text: Tanner McKee has 426 yards in two starts as Hurts' fill-in
stories.summary: McKee has completed 61.3% of his passes over two starts, with two touchdowns and one interception. In the loss to Dallas he went 23 of 35 for 211 yards, and Philadelphia led 21-20 in the third quarter. He starts again Sunday night.

stories.text: 0: sacks, QB hits and tackles for loss vs. Dallas
stories.summary: The Eagles defense recorded none of the three in the 38-21 loss and gave up 416 yards. Dallas ran for 204 yards, 155 of them by Javonte Williams. Philadelphia is tied for 30th in the league with three takeaways.

stories.text: Sunday night at Washington, 8:20 PM ET on NBC
stories.summary: The Eagles visit Northwest Stadium with the loser of this game sitting in last place in the NFC East. Philadelphia beat Washington 24-22 on Sept. 13. Watch whether Barkley and Smith can return from hamstring injuries.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders lose McLaurin for the season

stories.text: McLaurin is out for the year with a torn patellar tendon
stories.summary: The receiver got hurt in the 23-17 loss to San Francisco and went on injured reserve Wednesday. Dan Quinn expects rookie Antonio Williams to see more targets. Washington signed Van Jefferson from the practice squad and will lean on Stefon Diggs near the goal line.

stories.text: Daniels practices fully with left elbow, Diggs back to full
stories.summary: Quarterback Jayden Daniels was a full participant Wednesday and Thursday with a left elbow listing, and backup Marcus Mariota (knee) also went full. Stefon Diggs moved from no practice to full on Thursday. Tight end John Bates, defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw and Nick Allegretti did not practice, and Quinn said Kinlaw will likely sit. Friday designations were not yet posted.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels leads the league at 8.5 yards per carry
stories.summary: The quarterback has 213 rushing yards, fourth among quarterbacks, after missing about two and a half games with an elbow injury. Washington also has McLaurin and leading rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt out. Daniels' legs matter more with that supporting cast thin.

stories.text: 0-5: Washington's record last year in games after 8 PM ET
stories.summary: The Commanders have not won a regular-season primetime game since beating Atlanta 30-24 on Dec. 29, 2024. Sunday night's game against the Eagles starts at 8:20 PM ET. Washington also has the league's fewest giveaways, with two.

stories.text: Sunday night vs. Eagles, 8:20 PM ET on NBC
stories.summary: Washington hosts Philadelphia at Northwest Stadium coming off the bye. Both teams know the loser lands in last place in the NFC East. Quinn called it a game between two angry teams.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears pay two firsts for Jeffery Simmons

stories.text: Bears trade two first-round picks for Jeffery Simmons
stories.summary: Chicago sent its 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and a 2027 fourth to Tennessee for the All-Pro defensive tackle. The Bears get a 2028 fifth back. Simmons joins Grady Jarrett inside, and edge rusher Montez Sweat returns from a two-game suspension.

stories.text: Monangai misses another practice, but his odds improve
stories.summary: Running back Kyle Monangai sat out Thursday with turf toe and is on track to miss a fourth straight game. He was seen on an exercise bike Wednesday, and ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported he has a better shot this week. Linebackers T.J. Edwards and Jack Sanborn were estimated full participants, so both could return Monday.

stories.text: Simmons arrives as the league's top interior rusher
stories.summary: Jeffery Simmons has 28 pressures this season, the most of any defensive tackle, according to Next Gen Stats. He also has 3 sacks and 10 pressures when double-teamed, and 21 run stops. Dennis Allen gets a tackle who wins against both the pass and the run.

stories.text: 19: sacks for a Bears defense that ranks fourth in pressure
stories.summary: Chicago pressures quarterbacks at the fourth-highest rate in the league and has 19 sacks. The run defense is the soft spot at 4.4 yards allowed per carry, 26th by FTN's DVOA. Simmons targets that weakness.

stories.text: Bears visit Seattle on Monday night
stories.summary: Chicago plays at Lumen Field on Monday, Nov. 2 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Sam Darnold gets help up front after Seattle acquired guard Quenton Nelson from Indianapolis. Watch for a Simmons and Nelson matchup if both play.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions get stars back at practice for Vikings

stories.text: Lions try to end Minnesota's winning streak at Ford Field
stories.summary: Detroit hosts a Vikings team that has won 11 straight, dating to last season, and is seeking its 12th. The Lions are coming off a 20-17 win over Green Bay and want a third straight victory. Minnesota's coaches said the game will take their best effort and expect a loud building.

stories.text: Gibbs and St. Brown return to full practice
stories.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) were full participants Thursday after sitting out Wednesday. Kerby Joseph (knee) and Ennis Rakestraw (ankle) were limited both days. Game designations arrive Friday.

stories.text: Goff has 1,788 yards and no interceptions
stories.summary: Jared Goff has thrown for 1,788 yards and 14 touchdowns through six games without an interception. Vikings coordinator Brian Flores called Detroit's offense a major challenge. Goff gets a Minnesota defense that blitzes constantly.

stories.text: 153: yards for St. Brown against Green Bay
stories.summary: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught nine passes on 11 targets for 153 yards in the Week 7 win, then hurt his ankle. The Lions are reportedly optimistic he plays Sunday, and a full practice Thursday backs that up.

stories.text: Vikings at Ford Field on Sunday
stories.summary: Kickoff is Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. Minnesota allows the fewest points in the league. Detroit then travels to Miami in Week 9.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers hold off Panthers 27-19

stories.text: Packers beat Carolina 27-19 and stay in the NFC North race
stories.summary: Green Bay led by 17 in the third quarter, then saw Carolina cut it to one score with about five minutes left. Jordan Love threw three touchdown passes despite three Packers turnovers. The Packers improved to 5-3.

stories.text: Watson passes chest scare and returns
stories.summary: Christian Watson went to the hospital as a precaution after a first-half chest injury. Tests came back clear, and he returned to the game in the third quarter.

stories.text: Watson leads Green Bay with 113 yards
stories.summary: Watson caught a team-high eight passes for 113 yards, even with the chest scare. Love threw for nearly 300 yards and three touchdowns, with Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft each catching one.

stories.text: 39: rushing yards for Jacobs on 21 carries
stories.summary: Josh Jacobs is the first player since 2023 with at least 20 carries and fewer than 40 yards. Green Bay ran for just 66 yards as a team, yet Love completed 23 of 25 throws released within 2.5 seconds, a career high.

stories.text: Packers travel to New England on Nov. 8
stories.summary: Green Bay plays at the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox, per the league schedule. The Packers finished a stretch of three home games in 19 days Thursday and now hit the road.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings bring top defense to Detroit

stories.text: Vikings chase a 12th straight win in Detroit
stories.summary: Minnesota is 6-0 and has won 11 in a row dating to last season. Coach Kevin O'Connell said the game will take the team's best effort. The Vikings expect a loud Ford Field.

stories.text: Aaron Jones moves to limited practice
stories.summary: Jones (knee) went from no practice Wednesday to limited Thursday. Guard Joe Huber went full, tackle Brian O'Neill went full, and tight end Gavin Bartholomew (ankle) did not practice. Game designations come Friday.

stories.text: Jordan Mason steps in at running back
stories.summary: Mason returned from injured reserve against Indianapolis and ran 15 times for 68 yards. With Jones day to day, Minnesota may lean on him again Sunday.

stories.text: 12.3: points per game allowed, best in the NFL
stories.summary: Minnesota also ranks second in total defense at 252.8 yards per game. Brian Flores said the Vikings blitz at nearly a 70 percent rate. The offense has completed just 15 passes of 20 or more yards, 25th in the league.

stories.text: At Detroit on Sunday, then Buffalo on Monday night
stories.summary: The Vikings kick off at Ford Field on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. They host Buffalo on Monday, Nov. 9 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Minnesota wants to push the ball downfield more against Detroit.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons chase the NFC South lead in Tampa

stories.text: Falcons can grab the NFC South lead in Tampa
stories.summary: Atlanta sits at 3-4, tied atop a weak division with Carolina after the Panthers lost on Thursday night. A win at Raymond James Stadium would make the Falcons 4-4 and put them a half game clear before Carolina plays again. The Falcons have scored 31.0 points per game over their last five.

stories.text: Brian Robinson sits again, Deablo and Bowman return
stories.summary: Running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm), safety Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) and end Za'Darius Smith (rest) missed Wednesday but were limited Thursday. Right tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring) practiced on a limited basis both days.

stories.text: Drake London owns the NFL's third-down receiving lead
stories.summary: London has 38 catches for 616 yards, fourth in the league. His 266 receiving yards on third down lead the NFL, so Tampa Bay is expected to put cornerback Jacob Parrish on him. Penix can get him the ball quickly against a defense built to pressure.

stories.text: 31.0: Falcons points per game over the last five
stories.summary: Atlanta has scored 31.0 points a game across its last five, and Michael Penix Jr. has nine touchdown passes against one interception since returning to the lineup. That offense meets a Tampa Bay pass defense that ranks second in dropback EPA allowed.

stories.text: At Tampa Bay, Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Falcons play the Bucs at Raymond James Stadium. Watch Bijan Robinson, who leads the NFL with 907 scrimmage yards, against a Tampa defense that ranks third overall. Kyle Pitts has 629 yards and six touchdowns in eight career games against the Bucs.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Packers sack Young six times, beat Carolina

stories.text: Packers beat Panthers 27-19 as Young takes six sacks
stories.summary: Green Bay controlled Thursday night at Lambeau Field. Carolina fell to 3-4 but still shares the NFC South lead with Atlanta. Bryce Young took six sacks, and Jordan Love was 9 for 9 against the blitz to start the game.

stories.text: Rookie corner Lee hurt his hamstring in the first half
stories.summary: Carolina lost a rookie cornerback, identified only as Lee in the recap, to a hamstring injury in the first half. The Panthers also played without several starting linemen, per Yahoo's game summary. ESPN ran a postgame headline with Young saying his injured knee is fine.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard was the lone bright spot
stories.summary: Hubbard carried 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown. He also set a career high with seven catches, finishing with 119 total yards. He served as Young's safety valve while Green Bay pressured the quarterback.

stories.text: 3: Points Carolina scored off three takeaways
stories.summary: The Panthers forced three takeaways against Green Bay and turned them into only three points. The defense also allowed 354 net yards, and the offense could not take advantage of short fields.

stories.text: Home vs. Denver, Nov. 8, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Carolina has no game Sunday after playing Thursday. The Panthers return to Charlotte on Nov. 8 to host Denver. Watch whether the offensive line gets healthy after allowing six sacks at Green Bay.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Turnovers sink Saints heading into the bye

stories.text: Turnovers are the leak Saints must plug on the bye
stories.summary: New Orleans has 13 giveaways through seven games and a minus-4 turnover margin. The team has fumbled 11 times and lost seven. Tyler Shough has thrown six interceptions, and two more fumbles in Paris were overturned on review.

stories.text: Donaldson, Reid and Ruiz carry bye-week questions
stories.summary: Running back CJ Donaldson left the Paris game with a shoulder injury. Safety Justin Reid is recovering from an apparent concussion. Guard Cesar Ruiz returned to practice from a knee injury but did not start, and rookie Jeremiah Wright took his spot.

stories.text: Shough was efficient in Paris, apart from one throw
stories.summary: Tyler Shough went 30 of 38 for 278 yards and a touchdown against Pittsburgh. His one interception came in the red zone. Rookie receiver Barion Brown caught three passes for 57 yards, including a 49-yarder.

stories.text: 0-3: The Saints' record at the Superdome
stories.summary: New Orleans has not won at home yet this season, according to WWL. The Saints host Cleveland on Nov. 8 with a chance to change that. Their run defense ranks 29th, and Pittsburgh ran for 148 yards on them.

stories.text: Bye week, then Cleveland at home Nov. 8, 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: The Saints have no game this weekend. They return to the Superdome on Nov. 8 against Cleveland on CBS. Coach Kellen Moore said he will spend the bye finding ways to score points.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Winless at home, Bucs host Falcons

stories.text: Bucs seek first home win against Atlanta
stories.summary: Tampa Bay is 2-5 and has won two straight on the road, including a 43-13 rout at Carolina. The Bucs have not won at Raymond James Stadium this season. A win over Atlanta would give them their first home victory and a third straight win.

stories.text: Godwin, Goedeke and Irving do not practice Thursday
stories.summary: Receiver Chris Godwin Jr. (rest), tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) and running back Bucky Irving (rest) did not practice Thursday. Linebacker Josiah Trotter and edge rusher Yaya Diaby upgraded to full participation. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb) and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) were full.

stories.text: Rookie Josiah Trotter keeps leading in tackles
stories.summary: Trotter has led Tampa Bay in tackles in every game he has started and has 57 through six career games. He will take on Bijan Robinson, who leads the NFL in scrimmage yards. He missed Wednesday with an illness and returned to full practice Thursday.

stories.text: 11: Passes Mayfield threw in his return
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield attempted only 11 passes in the win at Carolina after missing three games with a thumb injury. That was the fewest by a Bucs quarterback in a win since the 1970s. The Bucs ran for 258 yards instead.

stories.text: Home vs. Atlanta, Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Bucs host the Falcons at Raymond James Stadium. Tampa Bay's rushing offense ranks third in the NFL, but its passing offense ranks 32nd. Watch whether Mayfield has to throw more if Atlanta slows Irving.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Power rankers push Arizona toward the bottom

stories.text: Cardinals drop in every power ranking after Denver loss
stories.summary: Arizona fell to 2-5 with a 30-16 home loss to Denver and slid in all seven power rankings that Cardinals on SI tracked. NFL.com dropped them eight spots to No. 30. Writers pointed to the worst goal-to-go possession of the season and a Bo Nix 62-yard scramble touchdown.

stories.text: Five Cardinals carry questionable tags into Dallas
stories.summary: Safety Andrew Wingard, cornerback Max Melton, defensive tackle Walter Nolen III, guard Jon Gaines II and quarterback Carson Beck were all listed questionable in the early-week report. Final designations come with Friday's practice report. Dallas lists Dee Winters, Drew Shelton and KaVontae Turpin as questionable.

stories.text: Kendrick Bourne is quietly on pace for a career year
stories.summary: Bourne has 25 catches for 234 yards through seven games, according to ESPN's numbers. That puts him on track for a career high in receptions. He gives a struggling offense a steady target on third down.

stories.text: 27th: Arizona's rank in pressure rate
stories.summary: The Athletic ranks the Cardinals 27th in pressure rate and 26th in quarterback hits. The same ranking puts their pass defense third-worst in the league. That combination let Denver's Nix beat them with his legs and his arm.

stories.text: At Dallas, Sunday at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Arizona (2-5) visits a Cowboys team at 3-4 at AT&T Stadium. Watch Beck's status and whether the offense finally finishes drives in the red zone. Seattle comes next, on Nov. 8 at 4:25 PM ET on Fox.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams get the league's only winless team

stories.text: Rams host winless Chargers without Davante Adams
stories.summary: Los Angeles (3-4) hosts a Chargers team that sits at 0-6, the only winless club in the league. Adams is out for at least a few more weeks, so the receiver room has to keep producing. The Chargers rank last in EPA per play, per SI's betting preview.

stories.text: Rams monitor McDuffie's groin, Landman back at full
stories.summary: Cornerback Trent McDuffie was limited Wednesday with a groin issue. Linebacker Nate Landman, in concussion protocol, practiced fully. Tight end Colby Parkinson (rib), lineman Coleman Shelton (hip) and long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.

stories.text: Stafford raves about Puka Nacua's physical play
stories.summary: Nacua caught 8 passes for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 35-21 win at Las Vegas. Stafford told the Pat McAfee Show that Nacua is as physical as any receiver he has played with. With Adams out, Nacua gets the lion's share of looks.

stories.text: 45: Puka Nacua's catches in five games this season
stories.summary: Nacua has 45 receptions for 485 yards and two touchdowns in five games, per SI. He has absorbed most of the targets while Adams recovers. Expect that volume to continue against a Chargers secondary dealing with hamstring issues.

stories.text: Home vs. Chargers, Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Rams meet the Chargers at SoFi Stadium. Chargers safety Derwin James Jr. did not practice and Jim Harbaugh said he suffered a rehab setback. Los Angeles then travels to Washington on Nov. 8 at 1 PM ET on Fox.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Shanahan owns the fourth-down call in Atlanta

stories.text: Shanahan defends going for it on fourth-and-10
stories.summary: After the 29-20 loss in Atlanta, Shanahan said he never considered a 41-yard field goal on fourth-and-10 because he believed San Francisco needed two touchdowns. The attempt ended in a sack. He also called a fourth-down jump offside "dumb" and put the sideline interception on Brock Purdy.

stories.text: McCaffrey has a mild hamstring strain, not a thigh injury
stories.summary: Shanahan said Christian McCaffrey's injury is a mild hamstring strain and that both he and the player are optimistic about a return for the Raiders game. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Nick Bosa also have a chance to return after the bye, but Shanahan promised none of it.

stories.text: Jordan Watkins' block springs Kaelon Black's touchdown run
stories.summary: Shanahan singled out receiver Jordan Watkins for sealing the only corner on Kaelon Black's long touchdown run in Atlanta. Black scored his first NFL touchdown on the play. The blocking was one of the few things the coach said worked on the day.

stories.text: 0: takeaways for San Francisco in Atlanta
stories.summary: The 49ers gave the ball away four times and forced none in the 29-20 loss. Two of the giveaways were second-half interceptions and two were fumbles on strip attempts. Shanahan said four turnovers to zero is hard to survive in this league.

stories.text: On bye, then home vs. Raiders Nov. 8 at 4:25 PM ET
stories.summary: San Francisco (6-1) is off this week. The Raiders visit on Nov. 8, with kickoff at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. The bye gives McCaffrey, Evans, Samuel and Bosa a week to heal before that game.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Nelson starts at guard in his Seattle debut

stories.text: Nelson will start at left guard Monday night
stories.summary: Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson makes his Seahawks debut at left guard against Chicago. Grey Zabel slides to right guard and Anthony Bradford moves to the bench, even after he played well in the 20-3 win over Kansas City. Chicago also traded for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons on Thursday, per PFT.

stories.text: Cross and Shaheed sit out, Leonard Williams limited
stories.summary: Left tackle Charles Cross and receiver Rashid Shaheed did not practice Thursday. Leonard Williams was limited with an Achilles issue. Macdonald sounded optimistic on Cross and said he is not an injured reserve candidate. Pregame listings earlier in the week had Cross as doubtful.

stories.text: Sam Darnold carries eight interceptions into Chicago
stories.summary: Darnold has thrown eight interceptions, four of them under pressure, while the offense ranks 24th in EPA per play. Chicago's pass rush is fourth in pressure rate. Seattle's line gets Nelson but may lack Cross.

stories.text: 1st: Seattle's defense in opponent yards per play
stories.summary: The Seahawks lead the league in yards per play allowed and rank second in defensive EPA per play. They also give up the fewest explosive passes. Chicago's offense has leaned on Caleb Williams, who has 1,020 passing yards in four games since his hamstring return.

stories.text: Home vs. Bears, Monday at 8:15 PM ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Seattle (4-3) hosts Chicago (5-2) on Monday Night Football at Lumen Field. Watch the Seattle front against a Bears defense that allows the most yards per play in the league. Arizona visits Nov. 8 at 4:25 PM ET on Fox.
